code.originalText: Eleven-week review: urea breath test, repeat endoscopy for ulcer healing, anemia, and surveillance planning

text.paragraph: Eleven-week review: urea breath test, repeat endoscopy, anemia, and surveillance. [S]

Mr. Natsume returns eleven weeks after diagnosis. He completed the 14 days of vonoprazan-amoxicillin dual therapy, missing no doses, with loose stools that settled after the course. He took vonoprazan each morning for the full eight weeks and stopped it two and a half weeks ago; he has had no epigastric pain since. He has had no tarry stools, vomiting or fainting. His back pain settled within two weeks. He takes iron every other morning and feels much less tired. He fasted this morning for the urea breath test and the repeat endoscopy with Dr. Abrahamsen-Ito. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 53.6 kg, BMI 21.2; pulse 72, blood pressure 118/74

About three weeks of gnawing epigastric pain, worse before meals and at night and eased by food, with two episodes of black, tarry stools ten days ago and iron-deficiency anemia; stable, Glasgow-Blatchford score 4; peptic ulcer suspected and urgent endoscopy booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at endoscopy; its timing echoes his documented stomach illness of May 1910 (D).

Gastric ulcer, 15 mm, on the lesser curvature at the angulus, with recent bleeding (melena) and a clean base at endoscopy (Forrest III); margin biopsies benign; Helicobacter pylori positive; synthetic modern diagnosis for his documented gastric ulcer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented gastric ulcer (D); the Helicobacter pylori cause is synthetic.
Helicobacter pylori infection (rapid urease test and histology positive; clarithromycin resistance mutation on biopsy PCR)
S — Synthetic finding at endoscopy; no historical claim is made about the organism in his illness.
Iron-deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 76 fL, ferritin 8 ng/mL)
Acute low back strain after lifting a box of books, without red flags, managed without NSAIDs because of the gastric ulcer; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.
S — Synthetic finding at the preventive visit; not a claim about his real health at this age.

list.item:
Helicobacter pylori eradicated (B96.81). The 13C urea breath test, done seven weeks after the antibiotics and more than two weeks after stopping vonoprazan, is negative: eradication confirmed. [S]
No further treatment.

Gastric ulcer, healed (K25.4). Repeat endoscopy shows the ulcer healed to a white scar with no residual ulcer; scar biopsies were taken. With the ulcer healed, H. pylori eradicated and no NSAIDs, he does not need long-term acid suppression. [S]
Scar biopsy result by phone.
No NSAIDs, now or later.

Chronic atrophic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia (K29.40). Open-type atrophy unchanged at endoscopy; no new lesion. [S]
Upper endoscopy yearly, starting one year from now.

Iron-deficiency anemia, corrected (D50.0). Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL and MCV 85 fL: corrected; ferritin 46 ng/mL, not yet 50. With the anemia corrected after the ulcer healed, colonoscopy is not needed now; screening begins at 45. [S]
Continue iron every other morning for three more months.
Blood count and ferritin in three months.
